qst.t002: Stars run from 1 to 10. Anything from ★8 upward expects a full team and finished gear.
qst.t005: Tags in brackets show the folder the quest lives in, for example [EP2] or [Halloween]. Event quests only appear while that event is running.
qst.t007: Counts come from the quest channels. Totals let you compare how dense a run is, which matters for experience and for material farming.
qst.t012: Open a quest to see every enemy and how many of them spawn.
qst.t017: Some enemies spawn in two waves; both are counted.
qst.t020: A 50 wave defence in the Mines.
qst.t021: A few quests list an enemy without a number in the original post. Those entries are left out rather than guessed, so a total can be slightly lower than the real count.
qst.t023: High end content is built for players who already have the gear. The development team's own advice is to work up through the easier content first.
qst.t032: Any area with an Area% level of 4. See the Server Systems page.
qst.t033: Quoting the development team on Silent Nightmare: the harder content was designed for players who already have the equipment and the practice. If you are not there yet, build up in the lower difficulty content first. It is not a step to skip.
qst.t034: Source: the Discord difficulty list maintained by the development team, and the monster counts posted in each quest channel. Quest and enemy names are kept in English.
qst.t037: Which quests match your gear, and how many monsters each one holds. Use the difficulty list to pick a target, and the monster counts to judge how long a run will take.
